sourceEvidence.heading: A Note on the Experiment
sourceEvidence.quote: The voice that says “I” in the pages that follow is a methodological persona.

sourceEvidence.heading: 1.1 What the Observer Who Does Not Kneel Sees
sourceEvidence.quote: The forms appear incompatible. Yet the bodies do recognizably related things: they repeat, synchronize, temporarily relinquish individual control, bear costs, transform space, regulate attention, and bind emotion to a story larger than the person.

sourceEvidence.heading: 4.1 The Rhythm That Dissolves the Boundary of the Person
sourceEvidence.quote: Synchronous movement, singing, shared pain, physiological arousal, and common attention can increase closeness, cooperation, and the sense of shared identity.

sourceEvidence.heading: 4.1 The Rhythm That Dissolves the Boundary of the Person
sourceEvidence.quote: The mechanism makes bonding possible; the symbol gives it direction and duration.

sourceEvidence.heading: 4.2 The Gift of Community and the Price of Absorption
sourceEvidence.quote: COMPOSITE SCENE A woman loses her partner. In the first days she cannot organize anything. The community arrives with food, answers the phones, prepares the ceremony, and tells her when to sit, when to speak, when to remain silent.

sourceEvidence.heading: 4.2 The Gift of Community and the Price of Absorption
sourceEvidence.quote: Years later, the same community asks her daughter to abandon a relationship considered forbidden.

sourceEvidence.heading: 4.2 The Gift of Community and the Price of Absorption
sourceEvidence.quote: Any community capable of offering intense support also has the power to withdraw that support.

sourceEvidence.heading: 12.2 The Chatbot, the Oracle, and the Manufacture of Revelation on Demand
sourceEvidence.quote: Availability, personalization, and fluency produce authority.

sourceEvidence.heading: 12.2 The Chatbot, the Oracle, and the Manufacture of Revelation on Demand
sourceEvidence.quote: A contestable human interpretation enters the corpus, is aggregated by the model, and returns in the impersonal tone of computation.

sourceEvidence.heading: 14.2 What Is Worth Preserving and What Must Be Disarmed
sourceEvidence.quote: Children and adults should understand the difference between experience, doctrine, institution, and identity.

sourceEvidence.heading: 15.2 The Questions That Remain Open After All the Explanations
sourceEvidence.quote: After I describe experience through prediction and neurochemistry, the problem of the referent remains.

scenes.title: An unfamiliar view
lines: The Animal That Prays explores why religion survives explanations of how it works.
Its imagined AI observer compares practices that familiar definitions often flatten.
A family honors ancestors, while a Buddhist monk attends to changing sensations.
Rather than isolate doctrines, the observer follows bodies, relationships, and shared meanings.
The book asks what becomes visible when belief stops being the only question.

art.composition: Two inhabited spaces unfold sequentially across a continuous wide view: a domestic ancestor-remembrance setting and a quiet meditation setting. Different gestures and objects retain distinct practices; do not blend traditions into generic exotic worship. A minimal observer reading annotation enters briefly, without a humanoid oracle or floating eye.
actionByLine: A family member carefully places a small offering beside an inherited portrait; a second person joins with quiet attentive posture.
Widen the view to another setting through a motivated shift of scale, showing the observer as a method of comparison, not a character claiming sacred authority.
The family tends its ancestor-remembrance place while a seated monk quietly attends to breath and posture; the two practices are visibly distinct.
Hold on the relative stillness and repeated actions; the objects of attention differ, with no floating memory/attention labels.
Return attention to the people and what they do; reserve the chapter title as the only scene heading.

scenes.title: What a shared rhythm does
lines: The comparison begins with bodies: people sing, breathe, and move together.
The book links shared rhythm with belonging, cooperation, and a larger felt identity.
A sacred chant and a secular refrain can both bring participants closer.
But their words connect that closeness to different stories and commitments.
Readers learn to separate a shared mechanism from the meaning it carries.

art.composition: A circular communal singing space becomes the foreground; a contrasting secular festival enters in a later shot. Human choreography and spatial spacing show synchronization. The source supplies composite comparisons, so no invented denominational costume or precise ritual is passed off as documentary reconstruction.
actionByLine: Begin with several participants finding a common pace; subtle breathing, head movement and hand gestures remain asynchronous before aligning.
Bodies turn toward one another, spacing narrows, and the group can complete a coordinated movement. No claim of one collective consciousness.
Shift to a secular outdoor singing crowd in everyday clothes; keep the recognizable bodily coordination but change the setting and story cues.
Return a brief comparative view: shared movement does not make the traditions or commitments interchangeable; avoid generic halos, neuron icons, and mystical beams.
Hold on individuals still distinguishable within the group, making shared coordination visible without erasing persons.
art.emotion: Tentative participation → warmth and shared energy → attentive distinction.

scenes.title: Care and the cost of refusal
lines: One composite scene follows a grieving woman supported by her religious community.
Neighbors bring food and organize the ceremony when she cannot manage.
Years later, that community pressures her daughter to abandon a forbidden relationship.
The same network can sustain a person and make refusal painfully costly.
The book follows this tension into institutions that authorize power or resist it.

art.composition: An inhabited domestic threshold replaces the prior abstract authority figures: neighbors arriving with a covered meal, a bereaved person seated with hands at rest, another neighbor helping with ceremony preparation. A time transition keeps the same recognizable people and place while changing the interaction into pressure on the daughter.
actionByLine: Introduce the source’s composite woman in a quiet domestic setting, supported by another person sitting beside her.
A neighbor offers food and another takes responsibility for an ordinary ceremony task; the woman receives concrete help.
After a simple Years later time cue, her adult daughter stands beside a partner while an elder objects through posture and gesture. Do not invent the basis of the prohibition.
The daughter turns between her partner and the same familiar group that previously offered care; show competing relationships, not a literal prison, gate or threatening weapon.
Open the physical spacing slightly for the unresolved question; retain the source distinction that communities can sustain or constrain, without painting all believers as coercive.
art.emotion: Grief and care → belonging → pressure and costly hesitation.

scenes.title: Who speaks through the answer
lines: Later chapters ask what changes when an intimate religious question reaches a chatbot.
A fluent answer can conceal whose interpretation has acquired authority.
The book distinguishes reported experience, its explanation, and claims about ultimate reality.
Start with the opening planetary scene, then explore the chapters on ritual and belonging.
Read it to understand religious life without reducing people to doctrines or mechanisms.

art.composition: Close, quiet nighttime scene of a person holding a phone beside a remembered loved one’s photograph; source-derived question, no invented chatbot theological answer. Then widen toward an open reading book with the actual source cover if suitable, keeping the reader and their questions central rather than displaying a conclusion machine.
actionByLine: The person types the source-grounded question Can the dead hear us?; show vulnerability through posture, no sensational distress.
An answer begins on the device; its interpretive origin is revealed as several differing source passages, grounded on the actual display, with no fake authoritative revelation text.
The display gives way to the person pausing; experience, interpretation and truth are separated in the narration once, without a warning badge or repeated caveat.
Place the actual opening page within a natural reading composition, using the chapter title Ten Minutes Before the Gods as an object label rather than an extra slogan.
Finish on the reader looking from the page toward the lived human settings invoked by the book; no claimed conversion, divine proof, or final metaphysical verdict.
art.emotion: Vulnerability → awareness of authority → curiosity and an earned reading invitation.

visualIdentity: Warm indigo, saffron, coral and sage; intimate human spaces, choreographed collective rhythm, a remembered domestic threshold and nighttime reading. No desks, provider archives, office cards, gate metaphors or repeated bell/footprint clip art.
visualAcceptance: One confident scene heading; all labels integral to source-specific objects.
Keep figures and labels above the full caption safe area through all travel paths.
Distinct participant identities, motivated gaze/hands/posture and quiet contrasts.
Do not blend different religious traditions into a invented universal ceremony.
Book is nonfiction; composite scenes explicitly attributed, religious authority is neither validated nor ridiculed.
